resale_co.name: Continuing Certificate of Occupancy (Residential CO)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspection fee is paid in advance. The application is void after 45 days.
requirements: 10-year sealed battery smoke detectors in each bedroom, within 10 feet of bedroom areas and the kitchen, and at least one per level including the basement and walk-up attic
CO detectors within 10 feet of bedroom areas and kitchens, at least one per level including basements and walk-up attics
Fire extinguisher rated 1A:10BC or 2A:10BC, no more than 10 pounds, visibly mounted in the kitchen or within 10 feet of it toward an exit
4-inch house letters and numbers visible from the street; tree limbs cut back at least 10 feet from the roof line
Handrails on stairways and stoops with 3 or more steps; guardrails on porches, balconies, raised floors and decks 30 inches or higher, spindles no more than 4 inches apart
No broken windows or doors, no holes in walls or ceilings, no structural or exterior damage, no leaking roof
Switch plates and outlet covers in place, GFI outlets within 3 feet of kitchen and bathroom sinks, light fixtures in place with no bare wires, secure covered breaker panel
Working range with anti-tip device and other appliances working; working heat (and air conditioning if present)
Hot and cold running water without leaks and flushing toilets; bathroom window or exhaust fan vented outside
Water heater relief valve extension within 6 inches of the floor (not closer than 2 inches); electric service wire and meter sound
No double-cylinder deadbolts on exterior doors; fire-rated door between an attached garage and the house
Sidewalks and driveways in good order without cracks or raised areas; pools, spas and hot tubs clean with proper security fencing
All code violations abated, all open construction permits closed, no rubbish or debris, all utilities on at the inspection
No more than 2 occupants per bedroom
Resale homes need a heater and chimney certification from a qualified contractor

fees.label: Continuing Certificate of Occupancy inspection (paid in advance by cash, check or money order)
fees.quote: Inspection fee is $100.00 payable in advance by cash, check or money order.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in the Borough of Woodstown Application and Continuing Certificate of Occupancy (mark "Resale", give the settlement date and the number of smoke detectors, CO detectors and extinguishers) and pay the $100.00 inspection fee in advance by cash, check or money order at the Housing Office, 2nd floor, Borough Hall, 25 West Avenue. Housing Official hours are Mondays 9a to 12p and Thursdays 1p to 3p.

evidence.quote: The Housing Official is responsible for Residential Certificate of Occupancy (CO). If a home within the Borough sells, it is required that a new CO is completed and filed at Borough Hall.
Housing Official Ed Ramsay 856-769-2200 ext. 112 / fax - 856-769-9462 housing@historicwoodstown.org Hours - Mondays 9a - 12p & Thursdays 1p - 3p 2nd Floor Borough Hall

REQUIREMENTS FOR A CONTINUING CERTIFICAE OF OCCUOPANCY ... All resale properties must have a heater and chimney certification from qualified contractor.

resale_co.notes: The Borough Housing Official page says a new CO is required when a home in the Borough sells. The application (Revised 1/24) has a "Resale" box and a settlement date line and says the application is void after 45 days and non-transferable; the requirements page (Revised 12-18-25) sets a $100.00 inspection fee payable in advance and lists a heater and chimney certification for resales. No separate re-inspection fee is printed (the application has a blank re-inspection fee line). Rentals also need a CO at each tenant turnover, annual landlord registration, a certified water test within 5 years, a lead-paint-free certificate within 2 years (an extra $50.00 lead certification fee) and current taxes, water and sewer (rental items).

requirements: Borough CCO list: 10-year sealed battery smoke detectors in each bedroom, within 10 feet of bedroom areas and the kitchen, and one per level including basement and walk-up attic
Borough CCO list: CO detectors within 10 feet of bedroom areas and kitchens, one per level
Borough CCO list (revised 12-18-25) still requires a 1A:10BC or 2A:10BC fire extinguisher, no more than 10 pounds, mounted in or within 10 feet of the kitchen

authorities.name: Woodstown Borough Housing Office (Housing/Code Enforcement), listed by the state for smoke detector compliance
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application or fee is published. The Borough Continuing Certificate of Occupancy inspection ($100.00) records and checks smoke detectors, CO detectors and the fire extinguisher. The NJ DCA online smoke certificate application does not offer Woodstown (the DCA marks it smoke-certificate exempt). Ask the Housing Official whether the CCO serves as the smoke/CO certificate.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety is Woodstown's fire code enforcing agency (LEA registry code S). The state fire directory (listed there as Woodstown Borough 1715) names "Woodstown Boro Housing" at 25 West Avenue, PO Box 286, (856) 769-1375 for smoke detector compliance, and the fire district feed used by the DCA online smoke application marks WOODSTOWN BORO-001 as smoke-certificate exempt, which the application uses to leave it out of the districts a private home can choose. The DCA's July 17, 2026 state towns list still marks Woodstown "SC", which conflicts with the feed. Taken together, the Borough Housing Office appears to handle the smoke/CO check through its $100.00 Continuing Certificate of Occupancy inspection; no separate smoke certificate fee is published. The Borough's own contact (856-769-2200 ext. 112, housing@historicwoodstown.org) is used rather than the directory phone. The Borough's "New Requirement for CO Smoke Alarms" handout (dated 2/22/2019) is a printout of a City of Hackensack page, so it is not used as Woodstown evidence. The Borough CCO list still requires a fire extinguisher even though the state removed it from the state requirement by P.L.2025, c.19.

other_items.label: Heater and chimney certification
other_items.detail: All resale properties must have a heater and chimney certification from a qualified contractor.

other_items.label: Open permits closed
other_items.detail: All open construction permits must be closed out and all code violations abated.

open_questions: Does the Borough CCO inspection serve as the smoke/CO certificate for a sale, or must the seller get a separate certificate (the DCA online route excludes Woodstown)?
Is there a re-inspection fee, and how far before closing should the CCO be booked?
